scope: Native Background SCI programmed-I/O fallback; unchanged DMA catch-up targets, stream protocol, CE scheduling and VMU worker

red.test: tests/test_retail_async_native_bounds.c linked against baseline production reader and stream

cases: raw and cooked 64-sector requests with continuously occupied guest DMA1, X and Y targets
interrupt-time foreign DMA takeover with unchanged guest owner
paused PIO resumes through EXEC/CHECK without any SCI interrupt
PIO returns to actual background DMA when guest DMA1 becomes idle
CRC reread and receive-ahead share one PIO allowance
REQUEST before-work completes an owned command, rejects replacement until CHECK acknowledges it, then accepts a new request
all requested bytes compared against the ordinary reference image reader
green.sanitizers: AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer for focused/native/CE host suites; detect_leaks=0 because runtime /proc access does not support LeakSanitizer

linked_background_artifact.note: Temporary label retains the final 12-character ID length for size verification; clean source commit and final package must be built separately.

remaining_limits: The limit bounds PIO data blocks, not elapsed time: legacy command, token-search and recovery wait windows are unchanged.
Preserving the DMA scheduling sequence does not prove hardware FMV behavior when a particular movie read falls back to PIO.
This reproduces and fixes a concrete long masked-work path; it does not prove that every console gameplay stall had this cause.
The user reported historical EDF FMVs as regular loading; the historical difference is not reclassified as Background loading.

independent_dma_only_comparison.scope: Three reads totalling 188 game sectors, interleaved IRQ/EXEC/CHECK; production baseline versus candidate with no PIO fallback
independent_dma_only_comparison.trace_inputs: DMA-start events, guest map events and cursor position
independent_dma_only_comparison.timing_claim: Deterministic scheduling and byte comparison only, not SH4 cycle or console frame timing.
